newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close up after correction.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close up after correction.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed up in active trade on Tuesday as buyers returned after a correction had brought shares down to realistic price levels, brokers said.
The index closed up 9.42 points at 727.32. Aitken Spence rose 3.75 rupees to 154, Commercial Bank 4.75 to 200 and Development Finance 12.25 to 272.50.
"The recent correction pulled stocks down to more realistic levels, which has attracted fresh buying," said Deva Ellepola of brokerage Jardine Fleming HNB.
Colombo stocks, which rose more than 15 percent in March and April due to improved investor sentiment, lost nearly four percent in a correction from April 23 to 25.
"From now on the all-share should move up in a more sedate manner, rather than gain by leaps and bounds like we saw in the recent rally," said Namal Kamalgoda of CTC Eagle Fund Management.
Brokers said investor sentiment was buoyed by good corporate growth expectations, low interest rates and a deal between the government and opposition to work together to solve the ethnic crisis.
Final turnover was 210.2 million rupees, supported by foreign buying of 3.8 million shares of Agalawatte Plantations.
